description: The figure presents an error/outcome breakdown comparing two models using two pie charts (Vanilla on the left and HCL on the right), each partitioned into four categories. In the left pie chart, the slices are labeled Atomic Skill Fail (dark teal) at 68.0%, Correct (medium teal) at 12.0%, Reason Error (light blue-gray) at 12.0%, and Question Misunderstood (very light gray/white) at 8.0%, with percentage values printed inside each slice. In the right pie chart, the slices are labeled Correct (medium teal) at 55.0%, Reason Error (light blue-gray) at 21.0%, Question Misunderstood (very light gray/white) at 14.0%, and Atomic Skill Fail (dark teal) at 10.0%, again with percentages shown inside the slices. A legend across the top maps the four labels to their colors, and neither chart shows exploded/offset slices; the slices appear arranged to place the largest segment prominently in each pie.
caption_used: Error analysis comparing the Vanilla model (left) and the HCL model (right) performance across four outcome categories. The left pie chart reveals that 'Atomic Skill Fail' dominates with 68.0% of errors, while 'Correct' responses account for 12.0%, and 'Reason Error' is marginally higher at 15.0%. The 'Question Misunderstood' category remains the least frequent at 8.0%. In contrast, the HCL model (right) demonstrates marked improvement, with 'Correct' responses comprising 55.0% of outcomes. However, 'Reason Error' persists at a concerning 28.0%, consistently surpassing the 'Atomic Skill Fail' rate, which stabilizes at 10.0%. The 'Question Misunderstood' category, though reduced, still represents 14.0% of errors. These results suggest that while the HCL model substantially mitigates 'Atomic Skill Fail' errors, it struggles to address reasoning gaps effectively, as evidenced by the elevated 'Reason Error' rate relative to the Vanilla model.
